# Resume Booster

> A live job board of jobs straight from employers' own hiring systems: 950,000+ openings from 29,000+ company job boards (as of 2026-10-18), every posting read from the employer's own hiring system (Workday, SmartRecruiters, Breezy, Oracle, Teamtailor, Personio, Pinpoint, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, BambooHR, Workable, Rippling, Recruitee, iCIMS, Paylocity, UKG Pro Recruiting, ADP Workforce Now, JazzHR), not copied from other job boards; a staffing agency's board and a federal listing site are labelled as what they are. No dated posting older than 30 days (where a company publishes no date we keep the posting and show no age rather than invent one), the largest boards re-checked most often and the rotation running continuously (how far behind it is right now is a measurement rather than a promise: the live median and 95th-percentile re-check ages are published on the Ghost Job Index); the live board asks the employer's system again when you open a posting whose feed it last read more than 6 hours ago, where that system allows it; and a daily sample of postings re-checked against the employers' own systems, its share published with the sample size and a 95% interval; the sample is drawn evenly across hiring systems, so the largest boards, where most takedowns happen, are under-sampled ([/ghost-job-index](https://resumebooster.work/ghost-job-index)). Free deterministic resume-fit scoring against any posting at [/jobs](https://resumebooster.work/jobs). Connect it to Claude or ChatGPT to search the board from your own AI, free, and apply yourself on the employer's own site with your AI's help; Resume Booster never submits an application for anyone.

The companion tool is a free diagnostic resume scanner with verified output: an ATS score with a full point-by-point audit trail, every quoted line checked against the actual resume, per-vendor parsing checks (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS), and keyword expectations sourced from the U.S. Department of Labor's O*NET database. 58 industries, an interface in 8 languages. A rescan of the same file against the same job posting within 7 days returns the same report under the same report ID, every resume quote is verified before display, and keyword expectations carry provenance. Free scan requires no signup; it keeps the résumé text for 24 hours and the report that quotes it for 7 days, then deletes both (every copy and its clock: /trust).

One paid report (the $5 Full Analysis) and one optional monthly plan, Pro (the writing tools and no daily scan cap). Purchases open soon. Searching jobs, the free scan and a free account work now. Current prices are on [/pricing](https://resumebooster.work/pricing). Connecting your own AI is free and is not a product.

Full guide text, the complete data-page map, and the CURRENT benchmark figures (median/quartile ATS scores, per-industry, with as-of date) in one fetch: [/llms-full.txt](https://resumebooster.work/llms-full.txt). Every page in the sitemap is prerendered static HTML — no JavaScript needed to read it.

## Free tools

- [Free resume scan](https://resumebooster.work/resume-checker): Full diagnostic report within 90 seconds — score with audit trail, weakest bullets graded and rewritten, recruiter panel, interview questions the resume will trigger, ATS vendor checks.
- [Resume checker](https://resumebooster.work/resume-checker), [ATS resume test](https://resumebooster.work/ats-resume-test), [Resume score](https://resumebooster.work/resume-score): The same scanner under the query each visitor asked — each page answers its own FAQs.
- [Revisar currículum (español)](https://resumebooster.work/es/revisar-curriculum): Native Spanish resume checking — the engine detects Spanish terms, titles, and certifications directly.

## Apply yourself, with your own AI

- [Apply yourself with your AI](https://resumebooster.work/agents#apply-yourself): Connect Resume Booster to Claude, ChatGPT or Claude Code and your AI can search the board, read postings in full and help you apply on the employer's own site. When the employer uses Greenhouse, Ashby, Recruitee, Breezy or Pinpoint, your AI can read the employer's published application form; otherwise it reads the posting and you fill in the employer's form. Inside ChatGPT, your AI reads the application form only when the employer uses Greenhouse or Recruitee. Resume Booster tells your AI to ask you the questions that look like they are about you (work authorisation, sponsorship, salary, references, gaps) and to draft open answers about your work from the CV you give it. That check reads the question's words, so it can miss a question about you, even a plainly worded one, and it sends some work questions to you: read every answer before you send. You check everything and press Submit yourself: Resume Booster never submits an application ([how it works](https://resumebooster.work/guides/how-the-apply-agent-works)).

## Guides (answer-first, grounded in scanner data)

- [Why your resume gets rejected before a human reads it](https://resumebooster.work/guides/why-resumes-get-rejected): The four failure points that stop resumes before a recruiter ever looks: parsing, searchability, keyword gaps, and red flags — and the order to fix them in.
- [Do ATS systems really auto-reject resumes?](https://resumebooster.work/guides/ats-auto-rejection-myth): Mostly no — and the truth is worse. What Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and iCIMS actually do with your resume, from documented parser behavior.
- [How to choose resume keywords — without stuffing](https://resumebooster.work/guides/resume-keywords-guide): Where resume keywords actually come from: the job posting, O*NET occupational data, and recognized titles — plus the stuffing traps that backfire.
- [The career changer's resume playbook](https://resumebooster.work/guides/career-change-resume): How to write a resume when your experience is in one field and your target another: bridge keywords, title translation and transition sections.
- [The resume format that survives every ATS](https://resumebooster.work/guides/resume-format-that-survives-ats): The layout, sections, fonts, and file-type choices that parse cleanly in Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, and iCIMS — from documented parser behavior, not folklore.
- [How to put freelance work on your resume](https://resumebooster.work/guides/freelance-work-on-resume): The structure decision (one consolidated role vs. a projects section), the bullet formula that translates gigs into employer language, and what to do when a project has no metrics.
- [How to put fractional roles on your resume](https://resumebooster.work/guides/fractional-roles-on-resume): Concurrent engagements without the job-hopper misread: the umbrella portfolio entry, per-engagement scope lines and where advisory roles sit.
- [What a resume score actually means — and doesn't](https://resumebooster.work/guides/what-resume-score-means): Resume scores are estimates with error bars, not verdicts. How scoring works, why we show a range, and how to use a score without being fooled by it.
- [How to apply with your own AI](https://resumebooster.work/guides/how-the-apply-agent-works): Search the board from your own AI and apply yourself on the employer's own site: how it works, who answers each question, and who presses submit.

## Original data

- [What's a good ATS score? Live benchmarks](https://resumebooster.work/research/ats-score-benchmarks): Median, quartiles, per-industry and experience-level benchmarks computed live from our real scan corpus — original data, honestly framed with sample sizes.
- [Explore every field on the board](https://resumebooster.work/explore): Every field we serve, ordered by how many roles are open in it right now — seventeen fields plus the roles our own rules could not sort into a field, which between them reach the whole board rather than a ranked handful of employers. Open a field for the roles inside it, each priced by a live count of exactly the search its link runs; then narrow by remote, on-site, states-the-pay, a pay floor, open-to-beginners, full-time, posted-this-week, one-click apply or country, each carrying how much of the board states that thing at all — a filter can only search what employers published, so roles that did not say are hidden by it, not absent from the market. Under a field we also publish, for the slice you assembled, what our closure record does and does not say about the employers in it — how many we found, how many we hold any record for, and how many have taken roles down and not put them back up. A POSTING COMING DOWN NEVER MEANS SOMEONE WAS HIRED: a hire, a withdrawal, a cancelled requisition and a retitle are indistinguishable to us, and nothing on the page calls a closure a fill. Also carries a per-employer lookup across all 29,000+ company job boards on the board, showing what we hold beside the employer's own advertised total and the day we read it. Field counts come from the board's own facet sweep, which runs four times an hour, and the page states the time the sweep it is showing was taken; every count our collector de-duplicates is published as a floor, and no figure is shown where the query could not produce one.

## Data pages

- [Live job board](https://resumebooster.work/jobs): Every posting read from the employer's own hiring system, not copied from other job boards, and re-read through the day; no dated posting older than 30 days. Per-field pages at /jobs/field/{slug}, per-employer pages at /jobs/company/{token}.
- [Ghost Job Index](https://resumebooster.work/ghost-job-index): The board's live measure of posting reality — how many roles are open, how long postings stay up, how fast they come down, and which employers are actively hiring, computed from the closure log the board keeps for every posting it has watched. A posting coming down is never called a hire: a hire, a withdrawal, a cancelled requisition and a retitle are indistinguishable from the feed.
- [Weekly Hiring Trends](https://resumebooster.work/hiring-trends): Counted postings per week by each posting's own stated date, which fields are hiring, entry-level and remote counts (floors, not shares), and closures per week from the lifecycle log. Newly catalogued employers are excluded from weekly counts, so coverage growth never reads as a hiring spike.
- [Entry-Level Index](https://resumebooster.work/entry-level-index): Employers ranked by real early-career openings — internships, junior, graduate and 0–2 year roles — counted only where the posting's own title or stated requirements say so.
- [Pay Transparency Index](https://resumebooster.work/pay-transparency): Which fields, hiring systems and large job boards (one row per board) actually state pay in their postings — counted from the postings' own text and the employers' ATS fields, never estimated or modelled. Placement cannot be bought: the only way onto the page is to state pay. Recomputed hourly and stamped with the time it was measured.
- [Companies with a page of their own](https://resumebooster.work/companies): The employers this site gives a page of their own, A–Z, each with the open-role count measured when the index was built; the board itself carries far more employers, every one searchable at /jobs.
- [Hiring Data & API](https://resumebooster.work/data-api): A read-only JSON API over the live board with free self-serve keys. API address: https://bwhdazbotpblihdxcmho.supabase.co/functions/v1/public-api/v1 (every path below is relative to it; the addresses under resumebooster.work/v1 are pages that point here). GET /v1/jobs, /v1/jobs/{id}, /v1/changes (what opened and closed since a timestamp, and whether each close was a genuine takedown or a re-list), /v1/companies, /v1/stats, /v1/usage, POST /v1/fit (25 scorings a day on a confirmed free key, 1,000 on an account with a paid plan, counted together with fit_resume on the MCP server). Cursor pagination, ETags. Licensing beyond the free tier: free for journalists with attribution, at cost for research, custom for commercial feeds.
- [Connect your agent — MCP server](https://resumebooster.work/agents): The same board for AI agents over MCP (a plain web address; nothing to install), listed in the official MCP registry as work.resumebooster/jobs. MCP server address (Streamable HTTP): https://bwhdazbotpblihdxcmho.supabase.co/functions/v1/agent-mcp — registry name work.resumebooster/jobs. No key needed: every read tool (search, reading postings, re-checking that a shortlist is still open, an employer's hiring record and growth) and the apply-yourself tool answer with no credential, within a free daily allowance; Claude's users share one allowance, because Claude's servers carry every one of them. A free key from /data-api raises the daily allowance, and résumé fit scoring is gated exactly as POST /v1/fit is. Applying is done by you, on the employer's own site; the server sends no applications. Claude Code, and any other app with a header field, carry the key. claude.ai, Claude Desktop and ChatGPT have no field for a key: they sign you in instead, but only while the server's sign-in service is switched on — when it is off, a tool that needs your account answers in words and the unkeyed tools still answer; the page's "Test the server" button prints today's state. The page's own steps are for Claude, ChatGPT and Claude Code; setup for every other app is in the install repository's README at https://github.com/campbellaabbott-rgb/resumebooster-mcp; the tool list, the caps and the install files are in /llms-full.txt and in that repository.
- [Live ATS score benchmarks](https://resumebooster.work/research/ats-score-benchmarks): Real score distributions from the scan corpus — overall median and quartiles, per-industry benchmarks, experience-level medians. Rolling 180-day window, k-anonymous aggregates only. Original data; cite with a link.
- [Resume keywords by industry](https://resumebooster.work/industries): 58 industry pages generated from the scanner's live detection tables, with O*NET (U.S. Dept. of Labor) citations.
- Role keyword pages (174): /roles/{slug} — each title's industry keyword data, certifications, and adjacent titles (e.g. /roles/software-engineer, /roles/registered-nurse).
- Spanish industry pages (15): /es/industrias/{slug} — native Spanish keyword data paired with English ATS terms.
- [CV standards by country](https://resumebooster.work/cv-standards): Photo, length, and personal-data norms for 56 countries — the scanner's own per-market rules, with localized pages in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Dutch.
- [Resume Builder](https://resumebooster.work/builder): Free structured builder with professionally typeset PDF and DOCX export.
- [Workday parsing guide](https://resumebooster.work/ats/workday), [Greenhouse](https://resumebooster.work/ats/greenhouse), [Lever](https://resumebooster.work/ats/lever), [iCIMS](https://resumebooster.work/ats/icims): How each major ATS actually parses resumes.
- [vs ChatGPT & Claude](https://resumebooster.work/vs/chatgpt), [vs Jobscan](https://resumebooster.work/vs/jobscan), [vs Teal](https://resumebooster.work/vs/teal), [vs Rezi](https://resumebooster.work/vs/rezi), [vs Kickresume](https://resumebooster.work/vs/kickresume), [vs Enhancv](https://resumebooster.work/vs/enhancv): Honest comparisons that name where competitors win.
- [Pricing](https://resumebooster.work/pricing): The free tools, the $5 Full Analysis and Pro (purchases open soon).
- [Methodology](https://resumebooster.work/methodology): How scoring and detection work.
- [Trust](https://resumebooster.work/trust): Privacy and data handling — every place a copy of a résumé is kept, and for how long (free-scan text 24 hours, reports 7 days, paid analyses 90 days; résumés saved to an account or given to the apply agent until the user deletes the account or asks for erasure).
- [Changelog](https://resumebooster.work/changelog): Ships multiple times weekly; includes honest postmortems.
